title: ArrayList versus array
context: What is the difference between an ArrayList and an array?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: An array has a fixed length, can hold primitives directly, and is fast and simple. An ArrayList is a resizable list backed by an internal array. It holds only objects, so primitives are boxed. It offers add, remove and generic type safety. ArrayList grows by copying into a larger array, so a known size is best given up front. Use an array when the size is fixed or for performance-critical primitives.

points.title: Fixed versus resizable
points.why: Array length can't change. ArrayList grows as needed.

points.title: Primitives and boxing
points.why: Arrays store primitives directly. Lists store boxed objects, which costs memory.
